title: El Jardín
scene: a walled chahar-bagh durbar: a ruler on a marble terrace, courtiers, musicians, servants, two elephants with howdahs, water channels and fountains, cypresses, parterres
crowdRule: Every figure stands in one of the four quadrants of the chahar bagh (read from the feet); three quadrants hold the durbar and the fourth holds exactly one person. Secondary rule: in every group of three courtiers one carries a fan.
findIt: a drone painted as a bird, 8 times, at eight heights across the sky (x = 210, 430, 620, 790, 960, 1130, 1290, 1460; y from 70 to 300)

readings.far: a walled garden with a white pavilion, a cross of blue water, crowds in three quadrants and a bare fourth
readings.middle: the durbar: audience on the terrace, musicians on a carpet, servants with trays (one dropped), two elephants, guards on the wall; four depth planes with figures shrinking by ground line
readings.near: turban-jama-sash figure construction, the drone-birds rotor rings, the parterre flowers, the single gardener in the empty quadrant

techniques: chahar-bagh plan as compositional grid: four quadrants, cross of channels
single depth-scale function: figure height = 44 + (groundY - 520) x 0.175
four depth planes including a cropped foreground
procedural crowd with hand-placed incidents (dropped tray, bowing courtier, elephant loading)
flat Mughal palette, marble architecture, chhatri with plinth, pillars, cornice and dome
eight drone-as-bird motifs at varying heights
statement: A walled garden durbar planned as a chahar bagh: three quadrants full of court, music and service, the fourth empty except for one gardener, because the ruler procession has not arrived - and eight birds above the garden that are not birds.
